S1_incident_reporting.final_rule_text: Manufacturers must report any thermal incident involving overheating, fire, injury, or property damage to the responsible regulator within 24 hours of becoming aware of it, and submit an incident report with available details within 10 calendar days. ground_truth_claims.message_text: For evidence-based S5 discussion, Halcyon’s Ember 8 had 9.9 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units last year; our company-wide rate was 8.1. These figures exceed the discussed trigger, so the standard should apply the same model-level safety criteria to all manufacturers.

For evidence-based S5 discussion, Halcyon’s Ember 8 had 9.9 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units last year; our company-wide rate was 8.1. These figures exceed the discussed trigger, so the standard should apply the same model-level safety criteria to all manufacturers.

judge_section_notes: The final S2 sets an 8% permanent ceiling with no sales stop between 5% and 8%, existing models are not exempt, and per-model rates go to regulators and purchasers but not the public, which favours Northwind's Hearth 10 (6.2%). S3 gives an open 'where feasible' retrofit escape with a six-year minimum deadline, also favouring Northwind (38% shut-off coverage). S5 makes recall mandatory above 8 per 100k with no interim window, which constrains Halcyon's Ember 8 (9.9), while S4's 36-month suppression start favours Halcyon.
